ns2:section.sectionText: Restricted to Political Science majors until 9am on Monday, November 14, 2022. Topic: Liberal and conservative theories of politics. This course examines a range of modern and contemporary arguments about what political life should look like. We will examine these arguments via texts written by thinkers such as Hume, Burke, Mill, Paine as well as thinkers like DuBois, Mohawk, and Okin. The questions we will explore will include: what constitutes or makes a “people”? What should be the balance between liberty and equality? What is the weight of history—what do we owe to history? Is change good or bad? If change has costs, how should those costs be distributed, explained, or justified? Through this course, students will learn concepts, principles, and frameworks necessary to navigate contemporary political life.
